title: Big Chief, Earl King and Wardell Quezergue
summary: He helped rearrange Earl King's Big Chief with Wardell writing parts for the other instruments; he has some sheet music.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Let me tell you. In the end. I'm trying to think. After Rip you went with, you did some things for Joe Asanto again. Yeah. And that was about, you did Third House from the Corner. Yeah. And Big Chief. Yeah. And well the Big Chief was a big thing. Earl King said he wrote that. He wrote that. Yeah.

Earl King, I just helped him out with it. Did he come up with the arrangement or did you? Well I had to rearrange some of the things. To fit what I was putting into his song you know. I had to rearrange the beat. And I had to rearrange the breaks. Well Wardell would give me a hand with it because he had to write the music for all the other instruments. I never find nobody could write for me you know. And Wardell's good, he can write for anybody. Oh but me? I don't know.
He sounded pretty good on that. Well I don't have any piano music.

Yeah. But all the rest of it, I have it. For Big Chief I have, for every instrument that was involved on the session, I have sheet music on it. Sax, clarinet. You've got it? You've got the sheet music? Yeah. What, Wardell gave it to you? I had it.
